entries.title: Auto mode blocks destructive commands by default
entries.paragraph: Auto mode now refuses git reset --hard, git push --force, and terraform / pulumi / cdk destroy unless those exact commands appear in the user's prompt. The release also adds deprecation warnings for retiring models, a /config --help command that lists every tunable setting, and fixes for thinking blocks, WebSearch, and cursor positioning.
entries.whyItMatters: Autonomous agents running in CI or staging can no longer accidentally wipe branches or tear down infrastructure.

entries.title: Direct config edits with /config key=value
entries.paragraph: A new /config key=value shorthand lets you change any setting inline without navigating menus. The release also adds a sandbox.allowAppleEvents option for macOS automation, a CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE env var for detecting running instances, and improved streaming of long paragraphs with auto-retry for mid-thinking connection drops.
entries.whyItMatters: Team setup scripts can now configure Claude Code non-interactively by piping config commands, making developer onboarding scriptable.

example.code:
# Set config inline — no menu navigation needed
/config model=claude-sonnet-4-6
/config autoApprove=true

entries.title: Agent teams simplified; Tool(param:value) permission rules
entries.paragraph: TeamCreate/TeamDelete tools were removed — agents are now spawned directly with implicit teams, reducing boilerplate in multi-agent workflows. Permission rules gain a Tool(param:value) filter syntax so you can allow a tool only when it is called with a specific argument, and nested .claude/ directory handling is improved.
entries.whyItMatters: Multi-agent orchestration code gets simpler, and fine-grained permission policies become expressible without custom hooks.

entries.title: Mid-stream connection drops now preserve partial responses
entries.paragraph: When a network interruption cuts a streaming response mid-flight, Claude Code now saves the partial result instead of discarding it. Mouse-wheel scrolling in WSL2 was also fixed, and long-conversation performance improved through better plugin loading.
entries.whyItMatters: Long autonomous runs that hit transient network blips no longer have to restart from scratch.

entries.title: Detect credits-required rate limits via SDKRateLimitInfo
entries.paragraph: Three new fields land on SDKRateLimitInfo: errorCode, canUserPurchaseCredits, and hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod. Together they let your SDK consumer distinguish a credits-exhausted limit from a rate-throttle and surface an appropriate billing prompt. Tool calls now also carry an icon_url in tool_use_meta, sourced from MCP server directory metadata. A bug where Remote Control sessions dropped file_attachments from inbound messages was also fixed.
entries.whyItMatters: Agents can now surface actionable billing guidance instead of swallowing a generic 429 error.

entries.title: Human-readable tool labels via tool_use_meta sidecar
entries.paragraph: Assistant messages now include an optional tool_use_meta object alongside each tool call with a displayName field. SDK consumers can render friendly labels (e.g. 'Search the web') instead of the raw wire name (e.g. mcp__brave__search). Also fixed: -p mode no longer exits before a completed background agent's notification is delivered.
entries.whyItMatters: UI integrations built on the SDK get polished tool display names without maintaining their own name-mapping tables.

entries.title: Typed permission-denial reasons for programmatic matching
entries.paragraph: Permission-denied advisory messages now carry a reason field typed as 'safetyCheck' | 'asyncAgent', letting SDK consumers branch on why a tool was blocked rather than parsing free-text strings. Spawn failures on a native binary now also explain a likely musl/glibc libc mismatch and suggest options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable as the fix.
entries.whyItMatters: Orchestrators can distinguish safety blocks from async-agent blocks and handle each appropriately without fragile string-parsing.

entries.title: SDK parity with Claude Code 2.1.183
entries.paragraph: This release tracks Claude Code 2.1.183, bringing the SDK to parity with the auto-mode safety guardrails — including blocking of destructive git and infrastructure commands — shipped in that version.
entries.whyItMatters: Applications embedding the SDK via the native binary get destructive-command blocking at no integration cost.

entries.title: Authenticated E2E encrypted Noise relay for remote executors
entries.paragraph: Remote executors now communicate over authenticated Noise-protocol channels, providing end-to-end encryption for all agent traffic without requiring a VPN. Cross-platform remote execution also now correctly preserves executor-native working directories, shells, and filesystem permission paths across app-server and exec-server boundaries.
entries.whyItMatters: Teams running Codex against remote dev environments get encrypted channels without configuring a VPN or SSH tunnel.

entries.title: OpenAPI spec sync
entries.paragraph: This release syncs the Node.js SDK with the latest OpenAPI spec, incorporating new endpoint shapes and parameter changes from the upstream specification update.
entries.whyItMatters: Projects targeting the latest API surface can upgrade immediately without waiting for manual wrapper additions.

entries.title: TypeScript main field and pnpm config fixes
entries.paragraph: Corrects the main field resolution in the TypeScript package, fixing import errors in bundlers that rely on strict module resolution. Also restores the pnpm monorepo configuration for the next distribution tag.
entries.whyItMatters: TypeScript projects using strict module resolution or pnpm workspaces should upgrade to avoid import path breakage.

suggestions.title: Audit your CI agent's allowlist for newly blocked destructive patterns
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.183 blocks git reset --hard, git push --force, and *destroy IaC commands in auto mode unless the prompt explicitly includes them. If your CI pipeline relies on any of these, add them to the permissions.allow list in .claude/settings.json or scope them to a dedicated agent that always receives the explicit instruction.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Agents that ran freely before may now stall on a blocked action mid-pipeline; a proactive allowlist review avoids silent CI hangs.
suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · 2.1.183 · Jun 19 — Auto mode blocks destructive commands by default

suggestions.title: Branch on SDKRateLimitInfo.canUserPurchaseCredits for targeted billing prompts
suggestions.paragraph: If your service calls the Claude Agent SDK on behalf of end-users, check event.info.canUserPurchaseCredits on a rate-limit event. When true, route the user to a billing page using the typed errorCode. When false, schedule a silent retry — no user action needed.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Generic 429 errors confuse users; typed signals let you show the right call-to-action on the first try.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.181 · Jun 17 — Detect credits-required rate limits via SDKRateLimitInfo

suggestions.title: Use tool_use_meta.displayName to render friendly tool labels in activity feeds
suggestions.paragraph: If your service surfaces an agent activity feed, read assistantMessage.tool_use_meta?.[toolUseId]?.displayName (SDK v0.3.179+) and display that instead of the raw MCP wire name. Fall back to the raw name when the field is absent for backwards compatibility.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Users see 'Search the web' or 'Read file' instead of opaque identifiers like mcp__brave__search.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.179 · Jun 16 — Human-readable tool labels via tool_use_meta sidecar

suggestions.title: Script team onboarding config with /config key=value
suggestions.paragraph: Use the new /config key=value syntax (Claude Code 2.1.181+) in your team onboarding scripts to set project-level defaults without menu navigation. Combine with a checked-in .claude/settings.json for committed settings, and use the CLI syntax only for developer-local overrides.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Onboarding a new developer goes from 'navigate three menus' to running a single shell script.
suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · 2.1.181 · Jun 17 — Direct config edits with /config key=value

suggestions.title: Evaluate Codex's Noise relay as a zero-config alternative to SSH tunnels for remote dev
suggestions.paragraph: Codex 0.141.0 ships E2E encrypted Noise-protocol relay channels for remote executors. If your service provisions ephemeral remote dev environments for agents, this relay can replace a VPN or SSH tunnel — the encryption is built into the Codex protocol layer, with no configuration required on the executor side.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Eliminating VPN requirements simplifies network topology and reduces the blast radius of credential leaks.
suggestions.tiesTo: Codex · 0.141.0 · Jun 18 — Authenticated E2E encrypted Noise relay for remote executors
